summary: Verified the Scorecard ID allocation bug fix end-to-end via Playwright (mobile viewport, Expo web preview). All 4 test cases PASSED. Format is hyphen-free `SC{YYYYMMDD}{NNN}`, per-date counter is monotonically increasing across new rounds, and resumed rounds preserve their original id. Two same-day rounds no longer collide.

test_1_format_and_uniqueness.note: Both live-sync POSTs for the same round carried the SAME id (correct upsert behaviour).

test_4_resume_does_not_reallocate.note: page.reload() + re-navigation to /round preserved the cached scId; no new allocation.

critical_code_review_comments: storage.ts:allocateScorecardId — read-modify-write on AsyncStorage is not atomic. In the current app the only callers are sequential (round-start, pair-start), so this is fine in practice. If ever two rounds are started concurrently on the same device, two callers could read the same `prev` and both write the same counter, yielding a duplicate id. Consider a mutex/queue if concurrent allocation becomes possible.

sheets.ts line 54 comment is slightly stale: it says the Apps Script assigns `SC-YYYYMMDD-NNN`. Since the client now always allocates and sends the id (hyphen-free), the comment should be updated to reflect that server-side assignment is only a fallback.

round.tsx: `syncLiveScorecard` still overwrites the cached scId with `res.scorecard_id` if the server echoes a non-empty value. Because the client now pre-allocates and sends its own id, the Apps Script should always echo the SAME id back — but if a legacy/misconfigured Apps Script returned a different id, the client would silently switch to it. Consider only accepting the server id when `priorId` is missing.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests intercept POSTs to script.google.com and return {ok:true,scorecard_id:''} to avoid touching the real Google Sheet.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified. `allocateScorecardId` in /app/frontend/src/lib/storage.ts + round-start block in /app/frontend/app/round.tsx now guarantee a hyphen-free `SC{YYYYMMDD}{NNN}` id, unique per round on the same day. Live-sync POST always carries the id in column A of the CSV. Backend Apps Script changes (upsert by Scorecard ID rather than Member ID) are the responsibility of the user — not tested here.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: two same-day rounds got similar server-assigned scorecard ids and the Apps Script upserted by Member ID, so round #2 overwrote round #1. Fix (verified): client now pre-allocates a unique `SC{YYYYMMDD}{NNN}` id via `allocateScorecardId(startIso)` at round start, persists it under `scId::solo::${roundId}`, and includes it in the FIRST live-sync POST. Per-date counter lives in AsyncStorage under `gs.scIdCounter::YYYYMMDD` and is atomic-per-caller (see code review note about concurrent starts). Resumed rounds reuse the cached id — no new allocation on reload.
